kangaroo-at-2020-01.prompt: Which tile below completes the wall next to it?

kangaroo-at-2020-02.prompt: Amira is travelling from Atown to Betown and passes two signposts along the road. One of them has a hidden number. What is this number?

kangaroo-at-2020-03.prompt: The board shown is made of small white and dark squares. After a quarter turn (90 degrees), what can the board look like?

kangaroo-at-2020-04.prompt: Ana lights a new candle every 10 minutes. Each candle burns for 40 minutes. After 55 minutes, how many candles will be lit?

kangaroo-at-2020-05.prompt: When the card is flipped over its top edge, we see the photo of the kangaroo shown. If instead we flip the card over its right edge, what will we see?

kangaroo-at-2020-06.prompt: Bia has the five coins shown: 1 real, 50 centavos, 25 centavos, 10 centavos and 5 centavos. She goes to the grocery store to buy a piece of fruit using exactly three coins, without receiving change. Which of the following prices can she **not** pay?

kangaroo-at-2020-07.prompt: In a garden, a bush has branches with seven leaves, or branches with four leaves and a flower. Janaina counted 9 flowers and 120 leaves on the bush. How many branches does the bush have?

kangaroo-at-2020-09.prompt: Five boxes contain 2, 3, 4, 7 and 15 balls respectively. Peter wants to move balls between the boxes so that every box has twice or half the number of balls of some other box. What is the smallest number of balls he must move?

kangaroo-at-2020-10.prompt: Two little mice, one white and one dark, leave at the same time towards the cheese along different paths, as shown in the picture, in which all the small squares are equal. The two arrive at the cheese at the same time. If the dark mouse runs 4.5 metres per second, how many metres per second does the white mouse run?

kangaroo-at-2020-11.prompt: The circles in the figure should be numbered from 0 to 10, each with a different number. The five sums of the three numbers on each diameter must all be odd. If one of these sums is the smallest possible, what is the largest possible value of one of the other sums?

kangaroo-at-2020-12.prompt: When Elisa the bat left her cave at night, the digital clock showed 10:20 (top picture). When she came back in the morning and hung herself upside down, she looked at the clock and saw 10:20 (bottom picture). How long did she stay out of the cave?

kangaroo-at-2020-13.prompt: On a distant island, 2020 kangaroos holding hands form a large circle. Each kangaroo is either brown and always tells the truth, or grey and always lies. Each one of them says the same thing: "One of my neighbours is brown and the other is grey." How many brown kangaroos are in the circle?

kangaroo-at-2020-14.prompt: Maria has exactly 9 white cubes, 9 light grey cubes and 9 dark grey cubes, all the same size. She glues all these cubes together to form a larger cube. Which of the cubes below is the one she made?

kangaroo-at-2020-15.prompt: The figures show five paths, drawn with the thickest lines, between the points X and Y. Which of these paths is the longest?

kangaroo-at-2020-16.prompt: Mary numbered the faces of three cards from 1 to 6 (one number on each side of each card). Using these cards, she can make three-digit numbers, for example 135 or 234. But some numbers cannot be made, like 126. Which of the following numbers can **not** be made?

kangaroo-at-2020-17.prompt: Which of the following rigid pieces of wire, when copied, can make a closed shape without any crossings, with the two pieces joined at their ends?

kangaroo-at-2020-18.prompt: Amelia sticks these six stickers on the faces of a cube: mouse, elephant, duck, ladybird, dog and fly. The figure shows the cube in two different positions. Which sticker is on the face opposite the duck?

kangaroo-at-2020-19.prompt: Beatriz and her five sisters are 2, 3, 5, 8, 10 and 17 years old. Beatriz writes these ages in the circles of the diagram so that the sum of the ages in the four corners of the square equals the sum of the ages in the four circles in the horizontal line. What is this sum?

choices.text: There is more than one possible value.

kangaroo-at-2020-20.prompt: Maria puts 4 litres of water in vase I, 3 litres in vase II and 4 litres in vase III, shown in the picture. Seen from the front, these three vases look the same size. Which of the following pictures could show the three vases seen from above?

kangaroo-at-2020-21.prompt: Inside the grey square there are three white squares; the numbers inside them give their areas. The white squares have sides parallel to the sides of the grey square. If the area of the grey square is 81, what is the area of the grey part not covered by the white squares?

kangaroo-at-2020-22.prompt: John made a construction with wooden cubes of the same size, with the three views shown (front, right side, above), using as many cubes as possible. Ana, John's sister, wants to remove as many cubes as she can without changing these three views. At most, how many cubes can she remove?

kangaroo-at-2020-23.prompt: A panel is made of 4 circles. When Lucy touches a circle, that circle and the circles touching it change colour from white to black or from black to white, as shown in the picture. Starting with all circles white, what is the smallest number of circles Lucy must touch, one after another, so that all circles become black?

kangaroo-at-2020-24.prompt: Which set of weights below balances the third scale in the picture?

kangaroo-at-2020-25.prompt: Ten people each order an ice cream: four vanilla, three chocolate, two lemon and one mango. As toppings they ask for four umbrellas, three cherries, two wafers and one chocolate gum — one topping on each ice cream. Since they don't want any two ice creams to be the same, which of the following combinations is possible?

kangaroo-at-2020-26.prompt: A three-digit number is called *balanced* if its middle digit is the average (arithmetic mean) of the other two digits. How many balanced numbers are divisible by 18?

kangaroo-at-2020-27.prompt: Janaina bought three toys, spending all her money. For the first one she paid half of her money plus 1 real; for the second she paid half of what was left plus 2 reais; and for the third she paid half of what was left plus 3 reais. How much money did she have?

kangaroo-at-2020-28.prompt: Dirce built the sculpture shown by gluing together cubic boxes with sides of half a metre. Then she painted the sculpture, except for the bottom (the base it stands on), with a special paint sold in cans. Each can paints 4 square metres. How many cans of paint did she have to buy?

kangaroo-at-2020-29.prompt: Vania has a sheet of paper divided into nine equal squares. She folds the sheet as shown in the picture, first with horizontal folds and then with vertical folds, so that the coloured square ends up on top of the pile. She wants to write the numbers 1 to 9, one in each square, so that after folding they are in order from top to bottom, starting with 1 on top. On the open sheet (shown), which numbers should she write in place of $a$, $b$ and $c$?

kangaroo-at-2020-30.prompt: The figure shows a map of some islands and the bridges connecting them. A navigator wants to visit each island exactly once. He started at Cang Island and wants to finish at Uru Island. He has just arrived at the black island in the centre of the map. In which direction must he go now to be able to complete his route? (On the compass, O = West and L = East.)

choices.text: There is more than one possible choice.
